title: Markets: Tuesday 3 November

morning.session_note: Weekday ASX edition · before the 10:00 open
summary: Brent futures fell 7.6% to settle at US$104.77 and WTI had its biggest daily fall since 27 July, as Washington and Tehran signalled openness to a deal ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/02/oil-prices-fall-as-iran-us-pursue-diplomacy.html)). On preliminary figures the S&P 500 ended 0.5% lower and the Nasdaq 1.1% lower, while the Dow rose 0.4% ([Reuters via StreetInsider](https://www.streetinsider.com/Market+Check/Wall+St+rises+as+oil+falls+heading+into+US+midterm+elections/27268508.html)).

S&P/ASX 200 futures were up 60 points (0.7%) to 8,926 near 7am AEDT after the index fell 0.6% to 8,856.5 on Monday (snapshot; [AFR](https://www.afr.com/markets/equity-markets/asx-to-rise-oil-plunges-anthropic-commits-to-1-3trn-spending-20261103-p61ar0)). Cheaper oil lowers fuel costs for Australian households and airlines.

The RBA decides at 2.30pm, with a 25bp rise to 4.85%, an 18-year high, priced at more than 80% on Monday ([AFR](https://www.afr.com/markets/equity-markets/traders-are-betting-the-rba-s-race-is-run-is-it-a-mistake-20261102-p61aef)). US midterm results start arriving from Wednesday morning Sydney time.

cards.headline: Brent falls 7.6% as Washington and Tehran signal a deal is possible
cards.takeaway: Brent's 7.6% fall took it below US$105 for the first time since early October, though analysts quoted by CNBC and Reuters said diplomacy headlines have faded before.
cards.key_figure: January Brent futures settle US$104.77 (−US$8.66, −7.6%), 2 Nov (CNBC/Reuters) · US$104.38 at 7.21am AEDT (snapshot)
cards.new_since_last_issue: Monday's close edition had Brent down 3.2% in Asian trade. New: the full US-session settle, WTI's biggest daily fall since 27 July, and Goldman Sachs' estimate of the war risk premium.
cards.what_happened: January Brent settled at US$104.77, down 7.6%, and WTI at US$96.46, down 7.4%, WTI's largest one-day loss since 27 July ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/02/oil-prices-fall-as-iran-us-pursue-diplomacy.html)). Brent traded below US$105 for the first time since early October ([Anadolu](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/economy/brent-crude-falls-nearly-8-below-105-as-us-iran-diplomacy-eases-supply-fears/4109065)). Trump said in his final midterm campaign speech that Iran wants "to make a deal and that could happen" ([Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/live-news/iran-war-news-trump-midterms-peace-deal-israel-november-2)).
cards.why_it_matters: Goldman Sachs estimates a risk premium of about US$27 a barrel explains most of October's rally ([Euronews](https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/02/oil-slides-on-hormuz-deal-hopes-but-trump-keeps-iran-strikes-on-the-table)). Lower fuel costs matter for Australian inflation on RBA day, and airline shares rose as oil fell ([The Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/02/oil-price-falls-amid-hope-of-a-breakthrough-to-end-iran-war)).
cards.market_reaction: Brent futures US$104.38 at 7.21am AEDT (snapshot). Gold futures +1.3% to US$3,949.2 (snapshot). In the US, United rose 6.5% and Southwest 4.4% in afternoon trade ([SMH/AP](https://www.smh.com.au/business/markets/asx-set-to-jump-on-rba-day-wall-street-rises-as-oil-prices-tumble-20261103-p61ar8.html)).
cards.priced_in: Partly. Goldman raised its end-2026 Brent forecast to US$105 from US$90 (Euronews), about where futures settled.
cards.what_to_watch: Any US response to Iran's two-day Hormuz proposal, US crude inventory data on Thursday morning Sydney time, and the 29 November OPEC+ meeting.

competing_views.view: Does not expect the risk premium to erode completely on diplomacy headlines alone.
Skepticism is warranted after many "false dawns" in recent months, as quoted by Reuters.
Raised its end-2026 Brent forecast to US$105 from US$90.

comparison.title: Did Brent fall 7.6% or 11.3%?
comparison.why_different: The 7.6% fall is the January contract's settle against its own Friday settle of US$113.43, as reported by Reuters via CNBC and the ABC. The snapshot's −11.3% compares January's price this morning with the expired December contract's final settle (US$117.64), so it spans the contract roll and overstates the fall. The ABC's −8.1% is a later quote at about 7.15am AEDT. The FRED spot series is an EIA assessment published with a lag (latest 27 Oct). The figures are not averaged.

cards.headline: Wall Street's early oil-driven gains fade as chip and tech stocks fall
cards.takeaway: The S&P 500 ended 0.5% lower on preliminary figures after being up 1.1% earlier; the Dow held a gain.
cards.key_figure: S&P 500 −0.5% to 7,542.3, Nasdaq −1.1% to 25,164.3, Dow +0.4% to 51,992.2, preliminary close 2 Nov (Reuters)
cards.new_since_last_issue: Monday's issue covered Friday's AI selloff. New: Monday's session, Marvell's US$115 billion deal for Lumentum and the October ISM manufacturing reading.
cards.what_happened: The S&P 500 lost 0.5% to 7,542.27 and the Nasdaq 1.07% to 25,164.32, while the Dow rose 0.43% to 51,992.19, on preliminary data ([Reuters via StreetInsider](https://www.streetinsider.com/Market+Check/Wall+St+rises+as+oil+falls+heading+into+US+midterm+elections/27268508.html)). The S&P 500 had been up 1.1% earlier in the session ([SMH/AP](https://www.smh.com.au/business/markets/asx-set-to-jump-on-rba-day-wall-street-rises-as-oil-prices-tumble-20261103-p61ar8.html)). Apple fell ahead of its results and Intel extended Friday's 29% drop (Reuters). Marvell fell 7.3% and Lumentum 12.8% in afternoon trade (SMH/AP) after Marvell agreed an all-stock deal with an implied enterprise value of US$115 billion, at 4.5 Marvell shares per Lumentum share ([Marvell](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1040/marvell-and-lumentum-to-combine-creating-a-category-leader-in-ai-connectivity)).
cards.why_it_matters: Marvell says the deal combines electrical and optical connectivity for AI data centres; it is expected to close in the first half of 2028, with Marvell holders owning about 67% (Marvell; [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/02/marvell-to-buy-lumentum-in-115-billion-deal-in-ai-data-center-bet-.html)). Apple and Palantir report after the US close.
cards.market_reaction: Airlines and cruise lines rose with lower fuel costs: United +6.5%, Southwest +4.4% and Carnival +5.5% in afternoon trade (SMH/AP). Oracle fell after filings showed a planned US$20 billion debt and share sale (Reuters).
cards.what_to_watch: Apple's results call at 9am Sydney time; Palantir also reports after the US close.

competing_views.view: Says demand for AI connectivity products is "exploding" and he does not see that changing soon.

cards.headline: ASX futures point to a higher open on RBA day
cards.takeaway: Futures point to a 0.7% rise after Monday's 0.6% fall; the RBA decision lands mid-session at 2.30pm.
cards.key_figure: ASX 200 −0.6% to 8,856.5, 2 Nov (snapshot) · futures +60 pts (+0.7%) to 8,926 near 7am AEDT (AFR)
cards.new_since_last_issue: New: the overnight futures move after oil's fall.
cards.what_happened: S&P/ASX 200 futures were up 60 points, or 0.7%, to 8,926 near 7am AEDT ([AFR](https://www.afr.com/markets/equity-markets/asx-to-rise-oil-plunges-anthropic-commits-to-1-3trn-spending-20261103-p61ar0)). The ABC put futures up 0.9% at about 7.15am ([ABC](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-03/rba-interest-rates-markets-live-coverage/107338216)). The index fell 0.6% on Monday (snapshot), led by materials and staples ([Market Index](https://www.marketindex.com.au/news/asx-200-live-today-monday-2nd-november)).
cards.why_it_matters: Gold miners led Monday's falls after gold hit a one-year low on Friday (Market Index); gold futures are now 1.3% higher at US$3,949.2 (snapshot). Travel and airline stocks rose overseas as fuel costs fell (SMH/AP).
cards.market_reaction: AUD/USD 0.7023 at the RBA's 4pm fix on Monday, −0.24% (snapshot).
cards.what_to_watch: The RBA decision and Statement on Monetary Policy at 2.30pm, NAB's full-year result on Thursday and Macquarie's half-year result on Friday.

cards.headline: China's central bank moves to support stocks after October's fall
cards.takeaway: The PBOC's swap operation on Tuesday could channel more than 100 billion yuan into Chinese shares, Australia's largest export market.
cards.key_figure: More than 100 billion yuan (about US$15 billion) applied for by 31 brokers and fund companies (PBOC via Reuters)
cards.new_since_last_issue: New: announced on Monday afternoon Beijing time.
cards.what_happened: The People's Bank of China will hold bidding on Tuesday under its swap facility for securities, fund and insurance companies, the third use of the tool since it was created, after the CSI 300 fell 8.5% in October, its worst month since early 2016 ([Nikkei Asia/Reuters](https://asia.nikkei.com/business/markets/china-s-central-bank-taps-liquidity-tool-to-aid-struggling-stocks)). Chinese state media also reported the operation ([China Daily](https://www.chinadaily.com.cn/a/202611/02/WS6ae85c65e4b06d4aa0566887.html)).
cards.why_it_matters: Chinese demand matters for Australian miners, which led Monday's ASX falls. The Shanghai Composite rose 1.1% on Monday (Nikkei Asia/Reuters).
cards.what_to_watch: The size of Tuesday's operation and China's services PMI on Wednesday at 12.45pm Sydney time.

competing_views.view: Says the move "sends another strong signal" of policymakers' commitment to market stability.

cards.headline: RBA expected to lift the cash rate to an 18-year high today
cards.takeaway: Money markets priced a rise to 4.85% at more than 80% on Monday; the RBA also publishes new forecasts at 2.30pm.
cards.key_figure: Cash rate 4.60% (snapshot) · hike priced at more than 80% on Monday (AFR)
cards.new_since_last_issue: Monday's issue gave the 78% Friday-close reading. New: pricing above 80% on Monday and the Melbourne Institute's call.
cards.what_happened: The money-market implied probability of a rise to 4.85% was above 80% on Monday ([AFR](https://www.afr.com/markets/equity-markets/traders-are-betting-the-rba-s-race-is-run-is-it-a-mistake-20261102-p61aef)). It would be the fifth increase this year ([ABC](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-03/rba-interest-rates-markets-live-coverage/107338216)). The decision and Statement on Monetary Policy are due at 2.30pm and Governor Bullock's media conference at 3.30pm ([RBA](https://www.rba.gov.au/coming-up/)).
cards.why_it_matters: The Statement on Monetary Policy, released with the decision, will carry the RBA's updated inflation and unemployment forecasts (ABC).
cards.priced_in: Mostly: the implied probability was above 80% on Monday (AFR).
cards.what_to_watch: Whether the board signals further rises, and ABS household spending on Wednesday at 11.30am.

competing_views.view: Expects a rise to 4.85%, describing higher rates as increasingly likely.
Expects a rise to 4.85% in November, citing inflation risks.

cards.headline: US factory gauge beats forecasts while price pressures ease slightly
cards.takeaway: ISM manufacturing rose to 55.5 in October, with production at its highest since November 2021.
cards.key_figure: ISM manufacturing 55.5 vs 54.5 in September and a 54.5 consensus · prices paid 75.2 from 77.9 (ISM)
cards.new_since_last_issue: New: the October reading, released at 2am Sydney time.
cards.what_happened: The ISM manufacturing index rose to 55.5 from 54.5, above the 54.5 consensus ([First Trust](https://www.ftportfolios.com/Commentary/EconomicResearch/2026/11/2/the-ism-manufacturing-index-increased-to-55.5-in-october)). Production rose to 59.0, its highest since November 2021, and new orders to 55.5, while the prices index eased to 75.2 from 77.9 ([ISM](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/manufacturing-pmi-at-55-5-october-2026-ism-manufacturing-pmi-report-302925617.html)).
cards.why_it_matters: Futures implied about a 72% chance of a Fed rise in December on Monday, with about 55bp of tightening priced over the cycle, down from more than 70bp a month ago ([FinancialMarkets.com](https://www.financialmarkets.com/article/australia-and-britain-may-raise-rates-this-week-odds-of-a-fed-hike-have-slipped-to-about-three-in-four)). ISM said tariffs, metals prices and oil-linked products are still driving the prices index.
cards.market_reaction: The US 10-year yield was down more than 2bp at 4.906% on Monday ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/02/us-treasury-yields-bonds.html)); Reuters said longer-dated yields moved lower as oil fell.
cards.what_to_watch: JOLTS job openings at 2am Wednesday, ISM services at 2am Thursday and October payrolls on Friday US time.

cards.headline: Qatari mediators go to Tehran as both sides describe talks as active
cards.takeaway: Trump says there is "no rush" to resume strikes but has not ruled them out; Iran sets conditions for reopening Hormuz.
cards.new_since_last_issue: Monday's issue covered the Doha talks and the two-day proposal. New: Trump's Monday remarks, Qatari mediators in Tehran, and a report that Gulf states were told to prepare for a possible US operation.
cards.what_happened: Trump said on Monday "there is no rush" to act, after Iranian negotiators left Doha on Sunday with a draft framework circulating ([Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/live-news/iran-war-news-trump-midterms-peace-deal-israel-november-2)). Qatari mediators travelled to Tehran on Monday evening, Reuters reported ([ABC](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-03/rba-interest-rates-markets-live-coverage/107338216)). Iran said it could reopen Hormuz within two days if the US meets its conditions ([Euronews](https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/02/iran-says-it-can-reopen-hormuz-in-two-days-if-us-meets-conditions)), with Qatar and Pakistan mediating ([Al Arabiya/AFP](https://english.alarabiya.net/News/middle-east/2026/11/02/iran-says-considering-twoday-plan-to-reopen-hormuz)).
cards.why_it_matters: The Wall Street Journal reported that the US told some Gulf states to prepare for a possible brief but intense operation after the midterms, and Trump has not made a final decision ([Quartz](https://qz.com/saudi-arabia-gulf-oil-exports-pre-war-rates-110226)). Vice President Vance and envoy Witkoff are urging diplomacy, Axios reported, while Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu and Defense Secretary Hegseth reportedly favour renewed strikes (Fox News).
cards.what_to_watch: A US response to the Qatari proposal and any follow-up meeting in the coming days.

competing_views.view: Says Iran wants a deal "more than they ever wanted" but warned the US could give Iran "the hammer".
Said "everything depends on the political rationality of Washington".

cards.headline: Gulf producers ship crude at about pre-war rates despite Hormuz risks
cards.takeaway: Tanker tracking shows Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Iraq and Kuwait exported 15.53 million barrels a day in October.
cards.key_figure: 15.53m b/d combined October exports, +10% (Bloomberg tanker tracking, via Quartz)
cards.new_since_last_issue: New: October tanker-tracking figures published on Monday.
cards.what_happened: Combined exports from the four producers rose 10% in October to levels in line with the start of the year, led by Saudi Arabia at 7 million barrels a day, according to Bloomberg ([Quartz](https://qz.com/saudi-arabia-gulf-oil-exports-pre-war-rates-110226)). Iran's exports stayed at zero under the US blockade. UAE Energy Minister Suhail al-Mazrouei said its exports had at times topped pre-war levels, Reuters reported (Quartz).
cards.why_it_matters: Physical supply from the Gulf has recovered even with Iran's exports at zero and talks unresolved. Many tankers switch off tracking signals, so actual flows could exceed the tracked figures (Quartz citing Bloomberg; [gCaptain](https://gcaptain.com/middle-east-oil-flows-near-prewar-levels-defy-hormuz-attacks/)).
cards.what_to_watch: The OPEC+ capacity assessment ahead of the 29 November ministers' meeting.

cards.headline: US votes in midterms, with strategists mapping outcomes for AI and bonds
cards.takeaway: Forecasts favour Democrats in the House with the Senate less clear; results start from Wednesday morning Sydney time.
cards.new_since_last_issue: Monday's issue covered final polls. New: JPMorgan's scenario probabilities and Reuters' survey of investor views.
cards.what_happened: JPMorgan puts a Democratic sweep at 66%, a Democratic House with a Republican Senate at 26%, and a Republican hold at 7% ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/02/the-midterms-are-here-how-jpmorgan-expects-the-market-to-react.html)). Forecasts point to Democrats winning the House, with the Senate less clear ([Reuters via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/analysisinvestors-gaming-out-congress-control-for-spending-ai-outlook-4990603)).
cards.why_it_matters: Investors quoted by Reuters expect a Democratic win to bring tougher oversight of AI, while a divided Congress raises shutdown and debt-limit risk. The Wall Street Journal reported a possible US operation in Iran after the vote (Quartz).
cards.what_to_watch: Results from Wednesday morning Sydney time; some races may take days to call.

competing_views.view: Puts a Republican hold at 7%, with the S&P 500 up 1% to 1.25%, and a Democratic sweep at 66%, with the index between −0.25% and +0.5%.
"A Democratic sweep would be neutral to mildly positive for the fiscal outlook."
A Republican sweep would validate the administration's fiscal agenda.

close.session_note: Weekday ASX edition · after the close
summary: The RBA lifted the cash rate 25 bp to 4.85%, the highest since 2008, on a 6–3 vote with three members preferring a hold. Its statement said the economy is slowing and house prices have fallen significantly, and Governor Bullock said it was "probably a good point to just take stock" ([RBA](https://www.rba.gov.au/media-releases/2026/mr-26-30.html); [ABC](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-03/rba-interest-rates-markets-live-coverage/107338216)).

The ASX 200 rose 0.27% to 8,880.5 as bond yields fell after the decision. Real estate gained 2.5% and discretionary 1.9%, while energy fell 3.5% after Brent's 7.6% fall on Monday; AMP dropped 9.2% after UBS cut its forecasts ([Market Index](https://www.marketindex.com.au/news/asx-200-live-today-tuesday-3rd-november)).

The Australian dollar fell 0.7% to US$0.6980 on the split vote. Brent futures edged up 0.5% to US$105.25 after US officials confirmed limited "defensive" strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island ([CNN](https://www.cnn.com/2026/11/02/politics/us-strikes-iran-qeshm-island)). Americans vote in the midterms today, with the first polls closing at 10am Wednesday Sydney time.

cards.headline: ASX 200 edges up 0.3% after the RBA hike as yields fall
cards.takeaway: Property, retailers and staples rallied on softer RBA guidance, while energy fell with oil.
cards.new_since_last_issue: This morning's briefing had futures pointing higher before the decision. The hike, the split vote and the sector reaction are new.
cards.what_happened: The S&P/ASX 200 closed at 8,880.5, up 0.27% from 8,856.5 (close snapshot; Yahoo Finance); Investing.com showed 8,881.6 in a day range of 8,856.5 to 8,909.1. Real estate rose 2.5%, discretionary 1.9%, telecoms 1.5% and staples 1.3%. Energy fell 3.5%, health care 0.7% and utilities 0.2%, while materials were flat (S&P/ASX sector indices, Yahoo Finance, about 4:06pm). Market Index said the market rallied after the hike as bond yields fell, and that health care tracked a 2.5% fall in US biotech stocks ([Market Index](https://www.marketindex.com.au/news/asx-200-live-today-tuesday-3rd-november)).
cards.why_it_matters: Rate-sensitive property and retail stocks led because the RBA dropped its tightening bias, which UBS's George Tharenou called "clearly dovish" ([ABC](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-03/rba-interest-rates-markets-live-coverage/107338216)). UBS also said expected FY27 ASX 200 earnings growth has fallen to just under 7% from almost 13% four months ago, according to Market Index.
cards.what_to_watch: US midterm results from 10am Wednesday, Woodside's investor day on Thursday 5 November, NAB's result on Thursday and Macquarie's on Friday.

cards.headline: AMP falls 9% on a UBS downgrade; airlines rise and energy slides with oil
cards.takeaway: Oil's fall lifted Qantas and Virgin and hit energy producers, while AMP extended Monday's slide.
cards.what_happened: **AMP (AMP) −9.2% to A$2.135** after UBS cut its earnings forecasts by 4.6% for FY26 and 4.8% for FY27, citing China Life Pension Company's September-quarter profit, which slipped 0.3% to RMB486 million; UBS's target is A$2.60 ([Market Index](https://www.marketindex.com.au/news/asx-200-live-today-tuesday-3rd-november)). **Virgin Australia (VGN) +8.1% to A$2.68 and Qantas (QAN) +6.7% to A$9.39** on cheaper fuel. **Energy:** Viva Energy fell 6.4%, Yancoal 5.9%, Whitehaven 5.4%, NexGen 5.4%, Ampol 4.7% and Woodside 3.4% to A$32.28. **Tech and property:** NextDC rose 5.6%, Zip 5.2%, REA 4.1% and WiseTech 3.2%; Mirvac rose 3.5%, Stockland 3.3% and Scentre 3.1%. Harvey Norman gained 5.8%. Closing prices and changes are from Yahoo Finance.
cards.why_it_matters: Banks were mixed: CBA rose 1.1% and Macquarie 1.4%, while Westpac and ANZ fell 0.9%. Macquarie Bank said it would lift variable home-loan rates by 0.25 percentage points from 19 November ([ABC](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-03/rba-interest-rates-markets-live-coverage/107338216)).

cards.headline: Seoul slides again on chip selling while Hong Kong edges up
cards.takeaway: The KOSPI fell almost 4% late in the session as memory-chip makers dropped, and Shanghai gave back Monday's gains.
cards.new_since_last_issue: The Asian session and China's move on foreign-currency deposit reserves are new since this morning's briefing.
cards.what_happened: Late in their sessions the KOSPI was down 3.9%, Shanghai 0.9%, and the Hang Seng was up 0.6% (close snapshot, Yahoo Finance). Tokyo was closed. At midday AP reported SK Hynix down 3.6% and Samsung Electronics down 2.9%, following Monday's fall in the Nasdaq, and said gains from China's market-support measures announced on Monday were short-lived ([AP](https://apnews.com/article/stock-markets-ai-earnings-oil-0d235af127a92c68da0cc2c45c028cef)).
cards.why_it_matters: China's central bank will raise the reserve ratio on foreign-currency deposits to 6% from 4% from 15 November, according to Reuters ([ABC](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-03/rba-interest-rates-markets-live-coverage/107338216)).

cards.headline: RBA hikes to 4.85% in a 6–3 split and signals a pause
cards.takeaway: The fifth hike of 2026 came with softer guidance, and the dollar and bond yields fell.
cards.new_since_last_issue: This morning's briefing expected a hike. The decision, the vote, the new forecasts and the market reaction are new.
cards.what_happened: The Monetary Policy Board raised the cash rate target to 4.85% from 4.60%, effective 4 November. It said the economy is slowing, housing prices have fallen significantly and unemployment has risen, and it now expects inflation to return to the top of the 2–3% band only in late 2027 ([RBA](https://www.rba.gov.au/media-releases/2026/mr-26-30.html)). The Statement on Monetary Policy has headline and underlying inflation above 3% until the end of 2027 and unemployment a little over 5% by the end of 2028 ([RBA SMP](https://www.rba.gov.au/publications/smp/2026/nov/pdf/statement-on-monetary-policy-2026-11.pdf)). Three members preferred to hold. Bullock said "I don't know what the next move will be" and that the board was not tightening because of the direct effect of oil prices ([ABC](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-03/rba-interest-rates-markets-live-coverage/107338216)).
cards.why_it_matters: Economists split on what comes next: Capital Economics thinks tightening is done, Betashares' base case is another hike in February, and CBA expects cuts in August and November 2027 (ABC). MNI reported a 35% chance of another hike by February in market pricing after the decision ([MNI](https://www.mnimarkets.com/articles/richer-after-rba-hike-35percent-chace-of-another-hike-by-february-1793680037524)). The dollar fell 0.7% to US$0.6980 (close snapshot), and Market Index said the 3-year yield fell 8 bp after the decision. Treasurer Chalmers said the war is pushing up inflation, while Opposition Leader Angus Taylor called inflation "homegrown" (ABC).

cards.headline: Brent steadies near US$105 after US strikes on Qeshm Island
cards.takeaway: Oil held most of Monday's 7.6% fall as US officials called the strikes limited and defensive while talks continue.
cards.new_since_last_issue: This morning's briefing covered Monday's fall on deal signals. The Qeshm strikes and Goldman Sachs' new scenario are new.
cards.what_happened: Brent futures were at US$105.25 a barrel at about 4:15pm Sydney time, up 0.5% from Monday's settlement of US$104.77 (close snapshot; Yahoo Finance). Three US officials told CNN the military carried out limited strikes on Qeshm Island in response to Iran firing at a US aircraft, describing them as defensive ([CNN](https://www.cnn.com/2026/11/02/politics/us-strikes-iran-qeshm-island)). Iranian state media reported explosions on the island and in Bandar Lengeh; there was no immediate official comment from Tehran, whose foreign ministry said earlier that "the ball is in the US court" on its Hormuz plan ([Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/3/explosions-hit-irans-qeshm-island-as-us-media-report-us-strikes-in-hormuz)).
cards.why_it_matters: Goldman Sachs raised its December Brent forecast to US$105 from US$90 and said Brent could peak at US$140 in 2027 if Gulf output stays 3.5 million barrels a day below its 2025 average, according to Reuters ([Moneycontrol/Reuters](https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/markets/brent-crude-at-105-wti-near-97-after-us-strike-report-on-iran-s-qeshm-island-clouds-peace-hopes-14067288.html)). Gold futures were at US$3,938.70 an ounce, down 0.8%, and COMEX copper at US$6.43 a pound, down 1.8% (close snapshot).

cards.headline: Americans vote in the midterms; JOLTS data at 2am
cards.takeaway: Europe is quiet, and US job openings come before results start arriving on Wednesday morning Sydney time.
cards.what_happened: Swiss October CPI is due at 6:30pm and a German 5-year note auction at 9:30pm Sydney time. The US cash market opens at 1:30am, and September JOLTS job openings and factory orders are due at 2am, with forecasts of 7.13 million and +1.2% ([Helious](https://helious.io/calendar/2026-w45); [Vedainvesting](https://vedainvesting.com/en/economic-calendar-today-3-november-2026/)). The first US polls close at 10am Wednesday Sydney time, according to Market Index, and New Zealand's September-quarter jobs data is due at 8:45am.
cards.why_it_matters: Apple fell about 3% in after-hours trade on its margin guidance, while Palantir beat forecasts and raised its outlook, according to Market Index. US October payrolls are due on Friday.
cards.what_to_watch: The US open at 1:30am, JOLTS at 2am and the first poll closures at 10am, Sydney time.

cards.headline: Open for Wednesday's briefing
cards.takeaway: Midterm results, Iran talks after the Qeshm strikes, and February RBA pricing stay open.
cards.what_happened: **US:** midterm results from 10am Wednesday Sydney time, and JOLTS overnight (Market Index). **Middle East:** whether the Qeshm strikes affect the Qatar-mediated talks; a US official told Fox News they did not mark the start of expanded strikes ([Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/3/explosions-hit-irans-qeshm-island-as-us-media-report-us-strikes-in-hormuz)). **RBA:** how the market prices February after the split vote ([MNI](https://www.mnimarkets.com/articles/richer-after-rba-hike-35percent-chace-of-another-hike-by-february-1793680037524)). **Companies:** Woodside's investor day on Thursday, NAB on Thursday and Macquarie on Friday; the Bank of England decides Thursday.
cards.why_it_matters: Each could move the ASX open, rate expectations or oil on Wednesday.
